title: Local repeated geometric functors and normalized repetition squares
statement: Let J and J′ be Grothendieck topologies on categories C and C′ essentially small in a common coefficient universe, B a sequence of commutative ring sheaves on J with transitions τ, uInv ⊣ uPush an adjunction of set-sheaf categories, and G a Geometry datum on the actual semilinear systems of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Let t be a finite-block monotone surjection and RX, RY its actual repetition packages [lem-pur-system-block-constructions]. There exist an OrdinaryInverseSystem P [lem-coef-ordinary-inverse-system] on the repeated towers using exactly G.inverseImage at t(m), and an OrdinaryDirectSystemCore K [lem-coef-ordinary-direct-system-core] using exactly G.levelPush and G.levelAdjunction at t(m). Thus K includes only the local two-component transition-mate equivalence, not a global Hom bijection. There are natural isomorphisms δ:G.pull ⋙ RX.repetition ≅ RY.repetition ⋙ P.pull and s:RX.repetition ⋙ K.push ≅ G.push ⋙ RY.repetition, identity on every component section. Evaluating δ and following P.component and G.inverseImage.modules of RY.evaluation is RX.evaluation followed by G.ordinaryPullEvaluation. Evaluating s and following RY.evaluation and G.ordinaryPushEvaluation is K.component followed by G.levelPush of RX.evaluation. No system adjunction, global unit/counit compatibility, K-injective resolution or derived comparison is asserted.

proof.text: For the actual geometric system datum G of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], at repeated index m use the specified algebraic inverse image G.inverseImage at t(m). Use its normalized coefficient-restriction comparison at t(n) ≤ t(m) to define every horizontal map. The original coefficient-sequence naturality identifies the reindexed coefficient maps, including identities within a block. Functoriality on underlying sheaves proves identity, composition and naturality; vertical descent gives the inverse-image sheaf on the sequence site. Exactness follows componentwise from the given exact module inverse images. This constructs the OrdinaryInverseSystem of [lem-coef-ordinary-inverse-system] without needing a new finite-limit hypothesis on uInv: G already supplies the exact module functors and normalized restriction comparisons.

proof.text: Construct the direct-image core with the fixed right adjoints G.levelPush at t(m). Its horizontal maps are uPush of the old underlying horizontal maps, conjugated by G.levelPushUnderlying. The normalized level adjunction unit verifies scalar linearity. Transpose a square for two arbitrary component maps using the set-sheaf adjunction: the defining normalized inverse-image transition identifies one edge, and the defining direct-image transition identifies the other. The two squares commute equivalently because set transposition is a bijection and forgetting module structure is faithful. This supplies the local transition_mate field of [lem-coef-ordinary-direct-system-core]; it does not assemble a global Hom equivalence.

proof.text: For inverse image, the ordinaryPullTransition equation of G identifies the old horizontal maps with the constructed ones. For direct image, transpose naturality of the original system unit through the component adjunctions, using ordinary_unit_evaluation. This identifies the old push transitions with the same local mates; equality is detected by faithful ordinary evaluations. Consequently on a repeated original system the preceding functors agree with the old ones at t(m), on arrows as well as objects. Their normalized component isomorphisms give the two displayed evaluation equations. They respect horizontal transitions by the constructions in the first two steps and vertical restrictions by naturality. Assemble them into δ and s, using [lem-coef-system-iso-assembly]; inverses and naturality follow by faithful ordinary evaluations. All component maps retain the actual underlying section carriers and therefore the comparisons are identity on sections. This applies also to the identity block map, repeated consecutive indices, zero coefficient rings, and arbitrary non-flat coefficient transitions.

theorem blockGeometricCore :
    ∃ (P : OrdinaryInverseSystem.{c, v, r}
      J (blockCoefficients B t) (blockTransitions J B τ t) J' uInv
      (blockCoefficients G.coefficients t)
      (blockTransitions J' G.coefficients G.coefficientTransition t)
      (fun m ↦ G.inverseImage (t.index m)))
      (K : OrdinaryDirectSystemCore.{c, v, r}
        J (blockCoefficients B t) (blockTransitions J B τ t) J' uInv
        (blockCoefficients G.coefficients t)
        (blockTransitions J' G.coefficients G.coefficientTransition t)
        (fun m ↦ G.inverseImage (t.index m)) P
        (fun m ↦ G.levelPush (t.index m)) (fun m ↦ G.levelAdjunction (t.index m)))
      (δ : G.pull ⋙ RX.repetition ≅ RY.repetition ⋙ P.pull)
      (s : RX.repetition ⋙ K.push ≅ G.push ⋙ RY.repetition),
      (∀ (M : Systems J B τ) (U : (ℕ × C')ᵒᵖ)
        (x : ((G.pull ⋙ RX.repetition).obj M).val.obj U),
        HEq (((δ.hom.app M).val.app U) x) x) ∧
      (∀ (N : Systems J' G.coefficients G.coefficientTransition) (U : (ℕ × C)ᵒᵖ)
        (x : ((RX.repetition ⋙ K.push).obj N).val.obj U),
        HEq (((s.hom.app N).val.app U) x) x) ∧
      (∀ (M : Systems J B τ) (m : ℕ),
        (evaluation J' (blockCoefficients G.coefficients t)
            (blockTransitions J' G.coefficients G.coefficientTransition t) m).map
              (δ.hom.app M) ≫
          (P.component m).hom.app (RY.repetition.obj M) ≫
          (G.inverseImage (t.index m)).modules.map ((RY.evaluation m).hom.app M) =
        (RX.evaluation m).hom.app (G.pull.obj M) ≫
          (G.ordinaryPullEvaluation (t.index m)).hom.app M) ∧
      (∀ (N : Systems J' G.coefficients G.coefficientTransition) (m : ℕ),
        (evaluation J (blockCoefficients B t) (blockTransitions J B τ t) m).map
            (s.hom.app N) ≫
          (RY.evaluation m).hom.app (G.push.obj N) ≫
          (G.ordinaryPushEvaluation (t.index m)).hom.app N =
        (K.component m).hom.app (RX.repetition.obj N) ≫
          (G.levelPush (t.index m)).map ((RX.evaluation m).hom.app N))
